reference.quote: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd restore Asia-Europe Suez routes as U.S. shippers watch capacity and costs

source_document.body:
The Pacific Maritime Association and International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 have reached a tentative contract agreement covering about 250 watchmen at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, averting an immediate strike threat at the busiest U.S. trade gateway.
The agreement, under federal mediation, remains subject to ratification by Local 26 members. The existing contract will be extended while that process proceeds, the PMA said.
In its announcement, the employers’ association thanked the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, the U.S. Department of Labor and Local 26’s bargaining committee for their work. It said the agreement would provide greater certainty for the ports, cargo owners, supply-chain workers and the regional and national economies.
No terms or timeline for ratification were disclosed.
The tentative settlement follows more than a year of bargaining. The previous contract expired in July 2025, and subsequent extensions allowed negotiations to continue. The latest deadline had been set for 12:01 a.m. Nov. 21, raising the prospect of a walkout if the parties failed to reach a deal or agree to another extension.
Union members had authorized a strike in late October. Federally mediated negotiations resumed Friday after an earlier bargaining session ended without a breakthrough.
Before the settlement, PMA said its offer included a $3,200 one-time bonus and wage increases that would lift average annual earnings for full-time watchmen from more than $170,000 to $198,000. The employers’ proposal also included continued fully employer-paid healthcare for active workers and retirees and higher pension benefits.
FreightWaves has reached out to Local 26 for comment.
Local 26’s watchmen provide security at six container terminals across the two ports. Their duties include controlling terminal-gate access, conducting security patrols and reporting safety issues.
There were concerns that cargo operations would be disrupted if other union workers honored watchmen picket lines.
PMA has said Local 26 represents roughly 2% of ILWU workers at the two ports.
Why it matters: The agreement reduces the immediate risk of a labor disruption at the nation’s busiest container port complex, where interruptions could affect cargo owners and businesses throughout the supply chain.
